- **1970-04-06:** Blood tests from the physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity [1].
- **1970-04-10:** A KSC management meeting decided the crew swap, announced at a press conference. Jack Swigert replaced Mattingly as command module pilot [2][3]. Mattingly's own note records the same change, from Apollo 13 command module pilot to an Apollo 16 assignment [9].

- **1970-04-17:** The crew splashed down, having used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat [4].
- **June 1970:** The Review Board, chaired by Edgar Cortright, published its report. It traced the explosion to tank No. 2 and recommended removing electrical equipment from inside the tank [6][7][8].
